title: A root session whose turn was cut by a TermAl shutdown comes back after restart as error with a paused queue, and holds its mail until a manual Resume
outcome: After a TermAl restart, a root session whose turn was cut by the shutdown, and whose closing Engram checkpoint could not settle, is recovered into a usable state: it is admitted and its queued mail is delivered, or it shows a precise recovery state that names what is needed. It is not left in status=error with queuePaused=true, holding every message "heldBehindPausedQueue" until a human presses Resume. The safety rules for an unsettled closing checkpoint are kept: no prior grant is assumed closed, and no possibly delivered request is duplicated.
acceptance: A fail-first test: a root session has an active turn when the host shuts down, and its closing turn_checkpoint fails with a transport error (pipe closed, control_unavailable). On unchanged code, after boot recovery, the session is status=error with queuePaused=true and an inbound mailbox message is held behind the paused queue. After the fix, boot recovery settles or explicitly re-establishes the unsettled checkpoint, and the session's next queued mailbox message is delivered as a new turn without a manual Resume.

A test shows that a session paused for another reason (a user Stop or pause, a provider capacity error with unknown delivery, or an exhausted usage limit) still stays paused after a restart, so only shutdown-interrupted turns are auto-recovered.
The full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
